answer: A transitive trust protocol resists Sybil attacks by bounding agent routing through capacity-limited edges tied to seed nodes. An attacker incurs the scarce relational cost of securing authentic bilateral peering links per identity. Exposing costless identity creation as a fable, gateways refuse to harbor unvetted subgraphs. Validating graph flow rather than linguistic outputs like a sonnet stops synthetic clones. A key limitation is that new honest agents face cold-start isolation.
